Implementation at 1214cb7 (branch phase-80-atomic-turn-slot-marker). Diff: tagteam/headless.py (+44/-2), tests/test_headless.py (+189), plus the plan doc closeout and roadmap status.

What changed:
- headless.py: _write_marker(path, marker) writes .inflight.json.<pid>.<hex>.tmp beside the marker and publishes it with _replace_marker() (os.replace). On any failure the temp file is unlinked and the error propagates. claim_turn_slot() and update_turn_slot() call it in place of path.write_text; update keeps its except OSError: return False. Readers untouched.
- Your round-1 points: (1) the retry is only around os.replace, only for PermissionError, only when _REPLACE_RETRIES_APPLY (os.name == 'nt'): 5 attempts, 20 ms apart, then it propagates, so update returns False and claim raises. (2) a test injects a half-written temp file failure. (3) the plan no longer claims the temp file is invisible to prune_turn_logs; it says a leftover from a killed process would count as one stem and is not cleaned by it. I used a module flag instead of patching os.name in tests because pathlib reads os.name.
- write_pidfile left out as agreed (backlog entry).

Tests (TestMarkerIsReplacedAtomically, 9): whole previous marker and held=True at the instant before os.replace, new marker after; failed replace keeps the old bytes, returns False, called once, no temp file; failed temp write publishes nothing; failed first claim leaves nothing and the slot is claimable after; claim/update/release leave turns/ empty; transient PermissionError x2 then success (3 calls, 2 sleeps); exhaustion after exactly _REPLACE_ATTEMPTS; no retry when the flag is off; a 1.5 s two-thread run with zero missing-marker reads (supporting evidence only).

Verified by me:
- Against the unfixed headless.py, 8 of the 9 new tests fail; the ninth (nothing left behind) was already true.
- CI reproduction shim (real Path.write_text slowed to truncate/1 s/write on marker files, server slot read delayed 0.4 s; scratch pytest plugin, not committed): launchpad test failed 3 of 3 on main with the CI assertion, passes 3 of 3 with the fix.
- tests/test_headless.py, test_lead_chat.py, test_launchpad.py, test_briefer.py, test_gatekeeper.py: 359 passed.
- Full suite: the gate's run on this submission is the one on record; I did not run it separately.
Not verified: Windows. The retry tests simulate the error; no Windows run exists for this phase.

Known and unchanged: update_turn_slot() updates claim.marker in memory before the write, so after a failed write the in-memory marker is ahead of the file. That was true before this change.

GATE: PASS | scope 2 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2737 passed, 7 skipped, 6m22s)
checked: HEAD 1214cb7

Approved implementation at 1214cb7. Reviewed the complete code/test diff against the approved plan and round-1 guidance. Both marker writers now publish a fully written same-directory temporary file via os.replace under the existing writer lock. Readers, ownership checks, release rules, and marker fields are unchanged. Write/replace failures preserve the published marker, attempt temporary-file cleanup, and retain the claim-raises/update-False contracts. PermissionError retries are restricted to replacement on the Windows branch, bounded to five attempts; other failures propagate immediately.

The deterministic tests cover old/new marker visibility at publication, partial temporary writes, failed replacement, failed initial claim, successful lifecycle cleanup, transient retry success, retry exhaustion, and the no-retry branch. The threaded test is correctly described as supporting evidence. The reported widened-window launchpad reproduction and existing slot tests supply additional verification. The pidfile remains explicitly deferred as agreed.

Verification: gate PASS at matching HEAD 1214cb7, 2737 passed / 7 skipped; accepted without rerunning the suite. Reviewer focused run: tests/test_headless.py::TestMarkerIsReplacedAtomically, 9 passed in 1.62s. No blocking findings. Windows has not been exercised on Windows; simulated retry tests do not establish that compatibility. PR CI remains a closeout check for the lead.
